title: Muru and the Sparkle Sneeze
markdown:
The warm sun shone on a mossy path. It wound through the Whispering Lantern Woods. Muru was a young ogre. His skin was green like moss. His heart was warm like the sun. He walked slowly. He liked these quiet times. The light shone through the leaves like little gold dots. The world made a low hum. Muru hummed a low, soft song too. It sounded like gentle thunder far away. He loved to hear the leaves whisper when a soft wind blew. He heard little bugs making a soft buzzing sound.

Muru lived in the Wobblecap Mountains. These woods were his favorite place. He liked to see little fuzzy caterpillars eating leaves. They chewed so slowly and steady. He liked to watch the glow-bugs. Their lights blinked on and off. They looked like shy stars coming out to play as the day grew softer. Muru always walked very carefully. His big, soft feet landed softly on the mossy ground. He did not want to disturb the quiet peace of the woods.

Suddenly, a little sputtering sound tickled Muru’s floppy ears. It sounded like a little water beetle trying to whistle a very quiet tune. Then came a small, fizzing pop! Muru peeked behind a big, soft mushroom. Its cap was a deep, earthy brown. There, in a patch of soft clover, was a creature Muru had never seen. It was a little dragon. It was no bigger than Muru’s two hands put together. Its scales shimmered like a rainbow soap bubble. They caught the fading sun. They flashed with little bright lights. The little dragon was sneezing! Each sneeze sent out a little puff of golden sparks. The sparks landed in puddles. They made a delightful fizz and a tiny puff of steam. The steam tickled Muru’s nose. Sneeze! Fizz. Sneeze! Fizz. The little dragon’s nose wiggled with each spark.

Muru blinked his big, kind eyes. He was very surprised. The little dragon looked a little wobbly. It seemed like it had just woken up. Its sparkly sneezes looked like tiny hiccups of surprise. Muru felt a gentle flutter in his chest. It was a warm feeling. How did such a tiny, sparkly thing get all alone in these big woods? Muru wondered if it had tumbled from its nest. Or maybe it wandered away from its mama.

"Hello?" Muru rumbled. His voice was soft and low, like gentle thunder far away.

The little dragon turned its head. Its big, curious eyes blinked slowly. It let out another little sneeze. A shower of sparks landed on a dewdrop on a clover leaf. The dewdrop shimmered like a tiny diamond. Muru smiled a slow, gentle smile. His kind eyes crinkled. "You seem a little lost," he whispered. His voice was a warm, low rumble. Muru decided he must help this little creature find its way home. Very carefully, Muru held out his big, mossy hand. His fingers were spread wide and gentle. The little dragon looked for a moment. Then, it rubbed its nose against Muru’s warm fingers. Its scales felt smooth and warm. Muru gently scooped it up. Its scales felt like warm, smooth pebbles from a river. He could feel the little dragon’s tiny heart thrumming softly in his hand.

"I think I'll call you Pip," Muru murmured. The name felt just right. Pip wiggled happily. He made a soft puff of sparks that tickled Muru’s chin. Muru chuckled softly. Pip’s sneezes were like little bursts of sunshine. They made the puddles dance with light. They made the tiny wildflowers around them seem to giggle. As they walked along the mossy path, Pip’s sparks lit up the darkening woods. The trees and ferns looked like a wonderland of soft light. They even found a patch of moon-moth silk. It shimmered with a soft, pearly glow. It was spun between two tall blades of grass. It felt as light as a whispered secret.

Muru walked along. Pip was nestled warmly against his chest. Pip’s little scales felt warm. Muru knew Pip wasn’t just lost. Pip was also a little bit lonely. Muru wanted to make Pip feel safe and loved. He patted Pip’s back gently. Pip made a soft, rumbling purr. It sounded like a tiny, warm motor humming.

The sun began to dip behind the Wobblecap Mountains. The sky turned soft shades of pink and purple. The shadows in the woods grew long. They stretched like sleepy giants. A gentle worry started in Muru’s heart. He wanted to get Pip home safely. He wanted to get home before the moon was too high. He wanted to get home before the woods became too dark.

They came to a place where the path split into many directions. The trails led into the growing dark. Muru wasn’t sure which way to go. Pip sensed Muru’s gentle worry. Pip made a little whimper. It sounded like a tiny sigh. Pip’s sparkly sneezes dimmed a little. They looked like little embers fading.

Muru sat down on a soft bed of moss. Pip was cradled gently in his lap. Muru felt a little bit helpless. He wondered if he could help Pip find his home. He wondered if they were truly lost. But then, he remembered Pip’s happy, spark-filled sneezes. He remembered how they made the puddles dance. He remembered how they made the flowers giggle. Pip just needed a little comfort. He needed reassurance. Muru whispered, "It's okay, little Pip. We’ll figure this out together." He held Pip close. Muru’s warmth and gentle rumble were a promise of safety. They were a soft, low lullaby.

Then, Pip sneezed. This time, it wasn't a fizzing shower of sparks. It was a soft, warm glow. It wrapped around Muru like a cozy hug. It felt like being wrapped in a warm, woolen blanket. As the glow pulsed, Pip pointed his tiny snout in a certain direction. That direction suddenly felt familiar. Muru knew the way now. He sighed a happy sigh. Relief washed over him.

Muru followed the gentle glow. He walked towards a clearing. A warm light flickered there. It was Barnaby, the Goblin jam-maker. Barnaby was tending a small, cheerful fire. The fire crackled softly. Then, from behind Barnaby, Muru heard a soft, worried coo. A much bigger dragon was looking around. Her scales were like polished amber. They gleamed in the firelight. Her big eyes were searching. Pip wiggled in Muru’s arms. He let out a happy squeak. Muru gently nudged Pip. Pip tumbled into his mama’s waiting embrace. The big dragon nuzzled Pip. She made soft, rumbling sounds. Pip sneezed a shower of happy, strong sparks. They lit up the clearing like a thousand tiny, dancing fireflies.

Muru watched. His heart felt full of quiet joy. A warm glow spread through him. He waved goodbye to Pip and his mama. He waved to Barnaby. Barnaby offered him a warm, gooey berry bun. Its sweetness filled the air. As Muru walked home, the lanterns in the woods seemed to glow a little brighter. Their light was a comforting beacon. The air smelled of pine needles and sweet berries. It was a lovely, comforting smell. He thought of Pip’s warm sneezes. He thought of helping a friend. It felt as warm and bright as the embers of Barnaby’s fire. Soon, Muru was home. A mug of warm, sweet cocoa waited on his bedside table. Its steam curled upwards like a gentle lullaby. Muru snuggled into his soft, mossy bed. The soft glow of his room reminded him of Pip’s happy sparks. He drifted off to sleep. He dreamed of gentle adventures and warm embraces. His heart was peaceful and content.
